item.title: FMA Survey: Outstanding volume of foreign currency loans falls to below €5bn in 2nd quarter.
item.dc:creator: FMA
item.description:
Only 3% of all lending to private households outstanding in either Swiss Franc or Yen.

Der Beitrag FMA Survey: Outstanding volume of foreign currency loans falls to below €5bn in 2nd quarter. erschien zuerst auf FMA Österreich.
item.content:encoded:
Adjusted for exchange rate effects, the outstanding volume of foreign currency loans (FX lending) to private households fell by 2.9% in the 2nd quarter of 2026, and now stands at €4.92 billion as of 30 June 2026. This amount makes up 2.7% of all loans to private households in Austria. These are the findings from the latest survey conducted by the Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) on FX lending.

Since the FMA banned granting new foreign currency loans in Autumn 2008, the outstanding volume has fallen by € 44.5 billion or 92% adjusted for exchange rate effects. At the height of the FX lending boom in 2006 almost one-third of all loans to private households (32%) were denominated in foreign currencies. This position was a risk for the entire Austrian banking sector during the Global Financial Crisis of 2008.

Practically all remaining FX loans (99.2%) are in Swiss francs (the remainder is almost exclusively in Japanese yen). At the end of the 2nd quarter, the Swiss franc exchange rate stood at 0.9224 CHF to the Euro. The Swiss franc has appreciated by 79% since 2008.

FMA estimates expect that the majority of the remaining bullet FX loans will mature between 2029 and 2033. Credit institutions are required to hold a meeting with affected borrowers at least annually. Borrowers should definitely take advantage of this opportunity.

Information about foreign currency loans to private households and the associated risks can be found here. The FMA Minimum Standards on FX Loans can be downloaded here.

item.title: Announcement: FMA imposes sanction on Liechtensteinische Landesbank (Österreich) AG for breaches of organisational rules
item.dc:creator: FMA
item.description:
FMA imposes sanction on Liechtensteinische Landesbank (Österreich) AG for breaches of organisational rules

Der Beitrag Announcement: FMA imposes sanction on Liechtensteinische Landesbank (Österreich) AG for breaches of organisational rules erschien zuerst auf FMA Österreich.
item.content:encoded:
The Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) has imposed a fine of EUR 244,000 against Liechtensteinische Landesbank (Österreich) AG. The reason is for breaches against the Securities Supervision Act 2018 (WAG 2018; Wertpapieraufsichtsgesetz 2018) in conjunction with rules set out in Delegated Regulation (EU) 2017/565. Liechtensteinische Landesbank (Österreich) AG specifically omitted to determine appropriate policies and procedures for the recommendations of suitable investment services and financial instruments to clients. In addition, it also omitted to determine appropriate training policies and procedures for submission of a legally compliant suitability statement. The penal order is not final.

Der Beitrag Announcement: FMA imposes sanction on Liechtensteinische Landesbank (Österreich) AG for breaches of organisational rules erschien zuerst auf FMA Österreich.

item.title: Announcement: FMA imposes sanction against Pierer Industrie AG for breaches of the Börsegesetz 2018
item.dc:creator: FMA
item.description:
FMA imposes sanction against Pierer Industrie AG for breaches against the Börsegesetz 2018

Der Beitrag Announcement: FMA imposes sanction against Pierer Industrie AG for breaches of the Börsegesetz 2018 erschien zuerst auf FMA Österreich.
item.content:encoded:
The Austrian Financial Market Authority (FMA) has imposed a fine of EUR 138,000 on Pierer Industrie AG as a legal person. Proceedings were concluded under the accelerated conclusion of proceedings pursuant to Article 22 para. 2b of the Financial Market Authority Act (FMABG; Finanzmarktaufsichtsbehördengesetz). The reason for the sanction is for a breach of rules under stock exchange law. The issuer specifically published its full annual financial reports too late for the 2023 and 2024 financial years respectively. The penal order is final.

Der Beitrag Announcement: FMA imposes sanction against Pierer Industrie AG for breaches of the Börsegesetz 2018 erschien zuerst auf FMA Österreich.

item.title: “Do you want insurance with that?”: the FMA explains about insurance cover for devices
item.dc:creator: FMA
item.description:
What consumers need to be aware of about insurance for devices.

Der Beitrag “Do you want insurance with that?”: the FMA explains about insurance cover for devices erschien zuerst auf FMA Österreich.
item.content:encoded:
You’ve chosen a new smartphone, an expensive pair of glasses, or a laptop, and as you pay in-store or online, you’re asked, “Do you want insurance with that?” The latest edition of the Austrian Financial Market Authority’s (FMA) consumer information series, “ Let’s talk about money” show how consumers can check whether additional cover matches their personal situation based on a few simple questions.

The initial decision rests on the following fact: an immediate decision is not required, device insurance can often be taken out independently of the purchase. Consumers should check, if possible without any time pressure, the types of damage actually insured. Depending on the contract, these may include damage caused by devices being dropped or broken, water damage, theft or technical defects. Consumers should be particularly vigilant about excluded cover as well as excess amounts. Wear and tear or scratches are frequently not insured.

Furthermore, they should also check whether additional insurance cover is really necessary. Statutory warranty claims or a manufacturer’s guarantee may exist for faulty devices. Household insurance or another existing insurance policy may also cover some types of damage.

The cost and length of contract are also significant factors for a decision. Seemingly reasonable monthly premiums can soon add up over the duration of the policy. The total costs should therefore be compared against the value and age of the insured device. Options to cancel the insurance are equally important, as some contracts are renewed automatically.

The current edition of “Let’s talk about money” can be found in English, along with all past editions on the website https://redenwiruebergeld.fma.gv.at/en. “Let’s talk about money” can also be found on Instagram under @redenwiruebergeld.
